main_body: A square farm plot: a crop field (wheat, cabbages, sprouts) seen from above, enclosed by a wooden post-and-rail fence on all four sides
top_band: none. A column through the field from row 16 down meets only crop rows (yellow wheat, green rows, round cabbages, soil furrows) stacked as a flat plan, with no top band and then a front face. The fence at the top has light-tan rail faces about 3 rows tall, with posts running vertically between them.
evidence: The main body is the crop field, which is a flat map-style plan. Its rows are laid out top to bottom as ground coverage, not as a standing volume with a top and a front face. The fence rails are flat tan bands with dark gaps and read as front-facing slats, with no horizontal top surface and no front face below one. Posts are vertical strips with no visible caps. The object is a ground patch with a border rather than a rack or frame, so the kind label fits poorly. It is a top-down plan, so it fails.

style.evidence: The crops use several greens, with shaded cabbages, leaf tufts, wheat speckle in yellows and cream, and furrowed soil grain. The wood fence has light, mid and dark browns, and its outlines are dark brown rather than black. The grey checker ground is broken up with dither, and no large flat fills appear. Each tile carries many colours, comparable to or richer than the reference stall and well.
